title: perf-canary: add burst spike scenario + neighbor protection assertions
author: Peter Holtz
description:
Context: Dedicated Burst introduces a new admission path (baseline -> burst pool) with strict caps/cooldowns and saturation gates. During pilot we need a repeatable canary that (a) produces realistic spike shapes, (b) validates admission behavior (admit/deny) matches the configured limits, and (c) ensures we don't regress neighbor SLOs (p99 drift) when burst is enabled. This PR adds a new load scenario to perf-canary that simulates a short-lived traffic spike from a single Dedicated tenant and asserts (1) burst admission success stays above the configured threshold when headroom exists, (2) burst reject rate spikes quickly when limits/cooldowns kick in (expected), (3) baseline traffic for a control tenant stays within p99 guardrail, and (4) routing fallbacks are exercised and counted when burst is denied.

What changed: Added scenario "dedicated_burst_spike_v1" that drives two tenants concurrently (burst-enabled tenant + control tenant) against the same region, with a 3-phase traffic shape: warmup (steady), spike (6x QPS step), cooldown (back to steady). The scenario uses per-request tags and response headers to attribute baseline vs burst and to differentiate deny reasons (limit, cooldown, saturation). Added assertions for: admit_rate_min, deny_reason_distribution, control_p99_max_ms, and max_neighbor_p99_drift_pct. Added optional "fault injection" toggle to force burst pool saturation (for staging) and verify circuit-break behavior results in clean denies (no tail-latency explosion).

Metrics + signals: The runner now scrapes the burst-related counters from the canary target (admit/deny counters + pool saturation gauge) and records them alongside latency histograms. All assertions are expressed in terms of those exported metrics to avoid parsing logs. We intentionally keep label cardinality bounded by using tenant aliases (tenant_a/tenant_b) rather than real tenant IDs.

How to run: 1) Configure env vars: CNY_TARGET_URL, CNY_API_KEY, CNY_REGION, CNY_TENANT_BURST (burst-enabled), CNY_TENANT_CONTROL (control). 2) Optional: CNY_BURST_SATURATION_TEST=true to run the saturation subtest. 3) Run: `make run SCENARIO=dedicated_burst_spike_v1`.

Rollout: This is behind the existing scenario allowlist; no default canary jobs are modified. SRE can enable it in staging first (nightly), then pilot regions.

Risks: (1) Flakiness due to noisy neighbors in shared staging; mitigated by using relative drift assertions + wider windows, and by gating the saturation subtest behind an env var. (2) Over-coupling to header semantics; mitigated by allowing either header or metrics attribution and skipping those checks if instrumentation isn't present.

Links: Linear ENG-4831. Related implementation PRs in `redwood` for burst admission + telemetry are referenced in the scenario README for context.
commits_summary: 1) scenario: add dedicated_burst_spike_v1 traffic model + phases 2) runner: metrics scrape for burst admit/deny + pool saturation 3) assertions: neighbor p99 drift + admit/deny thresholds 4) docs: scenario README + env var examples 5) CI: add lightweight unit tests for scenario parsing and assertion evaluation
changed_areas: Key files/areas: scenarios/dedicated_burst_spike_v1.yaml (new), runner/scenario_executor.go (traffic phases + tagging), runner/metrics/scrape.go (new burst metrics), assertions/burst_admission.go (new), assertions/neighbor_p99.go (new), docs/scenarios/dedicated_burst_spike_v1.md (new), .github/workflows/ci.yml (add unit test job matrix entry)
snippets: Illustrative snippet (scenario phases): `phases: - name: warmup duration: 5m qps: 20 - name: spike duration: 3m qps: 120 - name: cooldown duration: 10m qps: 20` and assertion example: `assertions: - type: burst_admit_rate_min window: 3m min: 0.85 - type: neighbor_p99_drift_max window: 5m max_pct: 10`
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): The shape looks good. Two asks: (1) ensure we fail fast if control tenant p99 exceeds threshold before the spike (baseline unhealthy), and (2) make deny reasons optional since header values changed between redwood builds during pilot. Peter Holtz (author): Updated. Added pre-spike baseline check and made deny reason assertion tolerant (skips if metric series absent; otherwise checks distribution). Mina Haddad (review): For fallback semantics, can we assert that when burst is denied we see non-zero fallback_count but not increased 5xx? Peter Holtz: Added `fallback_route_attempts_min` and `server_error_rate_max` assertions; fallback measured via routing metric if available, otherwise via response header. Keiko Yamamoto (review): Cooldown window seems aggressive. Will this flake across regions? Peter Holtz: Adjusted to check cooldown activation qualitatively (deny rate increases during spike tail) rather than hard-coded second-level boundaries; also widened evaluation windows. Allison Grant (review): Please confirm metric label cardinality is bounded. Peter Holtz: Using tenant aliases only; pool/model labels are disabled by default in the canary scrape config. Added doc note and a unit test that rejects configs that enable high-card labels together. Sean Gallagher: Approved. Mina Haddad: Approved.
ci_checks: CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), lint (pass), scenario schema validation (pass). One transient failure in integration smoke due to staging auth token expiry; rerun passed after refreshing CI secret.
release_notes: Internal: Adds new perf-canary scenario dedicated_burst_spike_v1 to validate burst admission behavior and neighbor p99 drift guardrails for Dedicated Burst pilot/GA readiness.
